summary: V6 implements the connected-water architecture required by the rejected V5 sprite review: an opt-in 11 by 9 procedural sheet is rebuilt from the same solver-sampled D4 contact shoulder and remains continuously attached to sampled live-water heights. The 160-triangle component is presentation-only, noncolliding, nonnavigable, shadowless, and cannot change forces, water samples, collision, map state, scoring, or progression. Native captures prove the geometry is live during a four-contact wrap/pin/recovery state. They also reject the current representation. High optical density exposes a large smooth translucent wall; photographic breakup collapses to a narrow fuzzy tuft; moving the breakup center beyond the boulder and retaining a faint connected body makes the candidate effectively disappear into the base surface. The current single sheet cannot simultaneously pass realism and gameplay-readability gates, so production remains selected and byte-identical.
